turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Next patient is Melissa Sanchez. Date of birth, 9/23/1962. Mrn: 5484367. She is being seen in office today for status post mitral valve repair done on 8/3/2020. At her previous follow-up on 9/17, we felt that she was doing quite well from a cardiac standpoint, and so we recommended she continue with the same medication. Ecg taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. Compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes, and please add in the history, patient has a history of mitral regurgitation and atrial fibrillation, history of diabetes, asthma, and recurrent chest discomfort with negative cardiac workup for coronary artery disease. Ms. Sanchez, it's good to see you again.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it's good seeing you too dr. Hughes. You look like you're doing well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I am, thank you. You too. You're looking great. How have you been feeling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Pretty good. I'm definitely feeling better, thank goodness. I was having a rough time before surgery, um, but I think I'm overall pretty good now though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Well, that's really good to hear. I'm glad. Are you having any new symptoms right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not really. But, you know, I'm still getting some chest pains sometimes, and my breathing gets shallow. But, I guess I'm learning what I can and can't do. Uh, so if I feel like that, if I'm, like, exerting myself, I slow down a bit which helps, and then when I go back to it later, I can usually finish whatever I was doing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So, it does go away though? How long does an episode seem to last?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, only a few minutes I guess. Then it disappears for a while. It's weird.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What is a while?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It goes away for a couple weeks. Um, so when it happens, I just take the day nice and slow, I don't push myself.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So, maybe it's a couple times a month you feel this way?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, just often enough for me to notice.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Understood. Okay. Are you taking your medications regularly?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh-. I've been trying to keep up with that. There's a lot of extra pills now, but I have a reminder app, so I do pretty well.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. That's great. And so, you're taking coumadin, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, also lasix and the atenolol.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Are you having any side effects from the medications at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not really. Uh, I notice that the atenolol is making me irritable in the beginning, but I guess I've gotten used to it, doesn't seem to bother me as much now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Well, that sounds good. Sounds like you're well on the mend. So, why don't I start out, um, with the physical exam, and just check you out.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're going to hear me describe things in detail or repeat things as I go to reference later for my notes.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay then. I'm going to be using my status post template, ms. Sanchez, please lie down on the table here and we'll get started. All right. Can you turn your head to the left. Head and neck no jvd detected. You can turn back now and just take a couple of deep breaths for me please. Okay, that's good. And lungs have reduced breath, but auscultation and percussion are clear. Okay. Breath normally, I'm just going to listen to your heart. Rhythm is irregularly irregular.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That's a funny statement. What does that mean?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, it does sounds kind of weird, right? It's when your heart doesn't beat with the correct rhythm, and whatever rhythm it doesn't have a pattern to it. So, it's part of the atrial fibrillation.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Wow, that sounds like a mess.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, it's not ideal. But, many people have a-fib are able to keep it under control with medicine and lifestyle changes.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Agh, I see. That's good to know.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So, s1 slightly accentuated, no s3. I'm going to touch your belly, and does any of that hurt.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about there? And your feet?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, great. And trace peripheral edema on extremities. All right ms. Sanchez, you can sit up now. So, it looks like your heart valves are working well and you are recovering from the surgery nicely.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yes. We are, we looked at your ecg taken earlier today, and we are seeing the a-fib, but it's being well controlled with the medicine, and you're taking coumadin, four milligrams, lasix at four milligrams a day, and the atenolol, you're taking that every day as well, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes. The 50 milligrams every day.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great. It sounds like you're well on your way to recovery.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Great.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, let's continue on your current meds. I'm glad that you're figuring out what your body can handle. Definitely try to keep active as that will certainly help.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'll do my best.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And that's about it. Do you have any questions for me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I do. When do I need to come back and get checked out?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, I don't think you need to come back soon. Everything from a cardio perspective is fine. So, I think let's do a followup in about six to nine months.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: All right, thank you. It was good to see you again dr. Hughes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You as well ms. Sanchez, do take care.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You too.
